question: When the Federal Reserve's policy-rate target changes by one percentage point, how much does the 30-year fixed mortgage rate change over the following twelve months, and how does that pass-through differ by period (for example 1990 to 2007, 2008 to 2015, 2016 to 2024)? Under the approved October 10, 2026 source replacement, use Federal Reserve policy-rate history, original FHFA mortgage statistics and CFPB/FFIEC HMDA, registering uncovered stretches as calibrated spread estimates.

title: How much of a policy-rate change reaches the 30-year mortgage rate
usableAnswer: A twelve-month pass-through coefficient (with its standard error) for each period, with the two series, the dates and the file or page each was read from.
whyItMatters: Home prices in the game move with the change in the 30-year mortgage rate. Where the game only carries a policy rate, the stand-in is passed unscaled and is labeled a stand-in; a measured pass-through would replace it.
